title: 'Greatly loved': Family members speak at first day of death inquest for Sask. man fatally shot by police in 2022
article: A death inquest for a 26-year-old man who was fatally shot by police in 2022 near Moose Jaw following a pursuit on Highway 1 began on Monday.
The inquest for Ryan Booker will be held at the Royal Hotel in Regina from June 23 - June 26.
The province said the coroner's inquest is to determine who died, when and where, and the medical cause and manner of death.
Recommendations from the coroner's jury may also be provided in an effort to prevent similar deaths in the future.
A jury was selected on Monday, hearing testimonies from four people, including Booker's partner, who was engaged to him at the time of his death.

His partner shared details of Booker's emotional state leading up to his encounter with the police. She stated that Booker took medication to treat his depression, but noticed he stopped taking it a few months prior to the incident.
On the day of his death, his partner said she and Booker's parents checked in on him at his camper in Moose Jaw and noticed he was using alcohol and drugs, while struggling with mental health issues.
Jury members also heard from Booker's parents. His mother told members she did not think he "understood how much he was loved."
"Everybody loved him, and told him he should've been in movies," his mother said tearfully at the inquest. "He's greatly loved by a lot of people."

When called as a witness, his father told the jury that he wished police gave him an opportunity to speak to Booker at the scene. When asked by the inquest council if he thought it would have made a difference in the outcome, he said yes.
"I think in a heartbeat, given the chance I would've got him out," said Booker's father.
"...If parents are there and want to talk to their kid, they should."
Family members of the 26-year-old continued to shed tears in the room as testimonies continued.
The fourth witness called on Monday was his partner's mother.
The incident that led to Booker's death occurred during the early morning hours of July 17, 2022, when a man was spotted with a gun and was allegedly uttering threats in a parking lot in Moose Jaw.
Police responded to the scene, but the suspect fled which led to a pursuit on Highway 1 ending near Belle Plaine when the suspect pulled over, leading to a six-hour standoff with officers.

Crisis negotiators responded to the scene, but the situation dramatically escalated and around 7 a.m., Booker was fatally shot by police after pointing a gun at officers and not responding to commands.
He received medical attention at the scene but was pronounced dead soon after.
After the incident, Moose Jaw police and Saskatchewan RCMP requested to have Saskatoon police conduct an independent investigation.
The inquest expects to hear from 15 people before wrapping up by Friday, by which point the jury can make recommendations to prevent similar deaths in the future.
- With files from David Prisciak
